points.why: Sets up in-training and trained stocks with hires in, graduates (half of trainees) between them, and 5% attrition out, all computed from start-of-month levels.
The table gives 10, 15, 17.5, 18.75 in training and 95, 95.3, 98.0, 101.8 trained, which match the expected values.
Attributes the dip to attrition starting at once while hires are held in training, and calls it expected rather than a failure.

Correctly derives the 20 and 200 equilibria and the slow approach, but never flags training time, the attrition rate, or faster early-tenure attrition as guesses to sensitivity-test; it only checks a timing convention and names levers.

pitfalls.why: New hires are held in training and only graduates count as taking tickets.
